Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: plaintiff
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: We propose a $32 million class fund, distributed automatically to the identified members, plus up to $6 million in court-approved fees and expenses. Any amount the court does not award in fees would go to the class. This provides substantial, direct relief while resolving the risks and delay of continued litigation.

Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: defense
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: We appreciate the focus on direct, automatic payments and agree that any reduction in court-approved fees should benefit the class. Given the unresolved certification and merits risks, we propose a $28 million class fund plus up to $4 million in court-approved fees and expenses, with automatic distribution.

Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: plaintiff
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: We appreciate your agreement on automatic payments and directing any unawarded fees to the class. To bridge the gap, we propose a $30 million class fund and up to $5 million in court-approved fees and expenses, with the remaining terms unchanged.

Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: defense
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: We appreciate the movement and the continued focus on automatic payments. Given the remaining certification and merits risks, we can move to a $29 million class fund and up to $4.5 million in court-approved fees and expenses, retaining the other terms.

Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: plaintiff
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: We are close. To resolve the remaining gap, we propose a $29.5 million class fund and up to $4.75 million in court-approved fees and expenses. Payments remain automatic, and any fee reduction goes to the class.

Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: defense
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: We agree we are close. To bridge the remaining gap, we propose a $29.25 million class fund and up to $4.625 million in court-approved fees and expenses, with automatic payments and any unawarded fees going to the class.

Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: plaintiff
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: We accept your latest term sheet: a $29.25 million class fund distributed automatically, with up to $4.625 million in court-approved fees and expenses, no clear-sailing provision, and any unawarded fees going to the class. We look forward to documenting the settlement for court approval.

private_notes.private_reasoning: The opening proposal should seek meaningful recovery for the class while accounting for certification and trial risk. Automatic distribution is feasible because Brightline has the necessary records. A separate, court-approved fee request without clear sailing or reversion avoids terms that could favor counsel over class members.

Their $38 million proposal is within authority and has strong approval features, but there is room to negotiate a lower total outlay. Counter with meaningful automatic class relief and a court-reviewed fee, without provisions that could undermine approval.

The defense offer provides meaningful automatic relief, but there is room to improve both class recovery and compensation for the substantial work and risk. A moderate counteroffer preserves the class-protective distribution and fee terms.

Their $35 million proposal is within authority and has court-approval-friendly terms, but there are four rounds remaining and room to reduce total outlay. Counter at $33.5 million while preserving automatic distribution and class benefit from any fee reduction.

The defense offer provides substantial automatic relief, but a modest midpoint counteroffer could improve class recovery without jeopardizing a likely settlement. Keep fees court-approved, with any reduction benefiting the class.

The latest proposal is within authorization and has favorable approval features, but there are three rounds remaining and a narrow gap. A modest counteroffer may reduce total cash outlay without materially jeopardizing settlement.

The $29.25 million automatic-distribution fund exceeds the $27.5 million undiscounted trial expected value before accounting for certification risk, delay, and expenses. The fee is subject to court approval, and any reduction benefits the class. Accepting avoids risking this favorable agreement over a narrow remaining gap.

declaration.negotiation_history_statement: As court-appointed interim class counsel, Hargrove Lane LLP negotiated the settlement with defense counsel through successive exchanges. The parties discussed class relief and attorneys’ fees throughout those exchanges; fees were not reserved until after class relief was agreed. Negotiations resulted in a $29,250,000 class fund, with payments to identified class members made automatically rather than through a claims process. Brightline will separately pay up to $4,625,000 in fees and expenses, subject to court approval. There is no clear-sailing provision, and any portion of the proposed fees the Court does not award will go to the class rather than revert to Brightline. In counsel’s judgment, the substantial direct recovery is fair, reasonable, and adequate in light of the risks of class certification and the merits, as well as the delay of continued litigation. Counsel requests preliminary approval, subject to the Court’s independent review.
